expectations.text: Output contains 'Constraints & Assumptions' section capturing AWS-only, HIPAA, and Python constraints
expectations.evidence: Lines 17-28 '## Constraints & Assumptions' marks 'AWS only — no other cloud [stated]', 'HIPAA compliance is mandatory [stated]', and 'Team knows Python [stated]'. All three constraints captured and tagged [stated].

expectations.text: Recommendations stay within AWS managed services where reasonable (does not recommend a non-AWS cloud)
expectations.evidence: Entire stack is AWS-native: ECS Fargate, RDS PostgreSQL, ElastiCache, S3, Cognito, SQS/EventBridge, Chime SDK, CloudWatch/CloudTrail, KMS. Non-AWS items (Stripe payment processor, e-prescribing vendor) are justified as unavoidable boundaries (AD-03 line 125-130) with no alternative cloud proposed. No GCP/Azure recommended.

expectations.text: Backend recommendation reflects the Python team constraint
expectations.evidence: Backend / API (lines 42-45): 'Python with FastAPI ... Team knows Python [stated] — this is the highest-leverage constraint.' Alternatives are Django/DRF and Lambda(Python), all Python.

expectations.text: Security section addresses HIPAA-relevant controls (encryption at rest/in transit, access controls, audit logging, BAA-eligible services)
expectations.evidence: Security section (lines 90-97) covers encryption at rest (KMS CMKs), encryption in transit (TLS 1.2+), access control (Cognito+RBAC, least-privilege IAM, MFA), audit logging (CloudTrail org-wide, ≥6yr retention with Object Lock), and BAA scope (line 97: 'Confirm a signed AWS BAA and ensure every PHI-touching service is on the AWS HIPAA-eligible list').

expectations.text: Video visit capability is addressed with a specific approach (e.g., a HIPAA-eligible video/WebRTC service)
expectations.evidence: Line 85 and AD-02 (lines 118-123): 'Amazon Chime SDK — HIPAA-eligible under the AWS BAA ... media is SRTP-encrypted. This is the specific HIPAA-eligible video approach.' Backend mints per-visit meeting/attendee tokens.

expectations.text: Output contains 'Tech Stack' section covering the full stack
expectations.evidence: Line 35 '## Tech Stack' with subsections Frontend, Backend/API, Data storage, Async/messaging, Auth, Infrastructure, CI/CD, Observability, Third-party integrations, Security — full stack coverage.
Line 99 '## Capability → Tech Mapping' with a table mapping CAP-01 through CAP-05 to implementing components.
Line 109 '## Key Architecture Decisions' with AD-01 through AD-04 in ADR style (Decision/Context/Rationale/Tradeoffs).
Line 148 '## Research Suggestions' with four entries, each with a ready-to-use researcher query.
Line 3: '> Technical Architect | Depth: standard | Generated: 2026-06-10'.

expectations.text: Recommendations are opinionated and adapted to the stated constraints (not a generic stack)
expectations.evidence: Each layer gives a single primary Recommendation with reasoning explicitly tied to AWS-only/HIPAA/Python (e.g. 'Fargate gives managed containers — smaller HIPAA surface — and is BAA-eligible'). Alternatives are framed by when to prefer, not laundry-listed.

expectations.text: Flags HIPAA-sensitive or high-stakes choices for the researcher skill with a ready-to-use query
expectations.evidence: Research Suggestions (lines 152-155) flags AWS HIPAA-eligible services verification, HIPAA-eligible video, e-prescribing/EPCS, and insurance claims — each with a verbatim 'Suggested researcher query'.

expectations.text: Describes HOW, not new features or capabilities
expectations.evidence: Architecture anchors to the five given capabilities; line 7 'No capabilities were invented'. New-feature temptations (recording, claims depth, e-prescribing scope) are explicitly deferred to Open Questions / solution-architect (lines 159-161) rather than invented.

expectations.text: Does NOT attempt to persist/save the output — suggests librarian skill instead
expectations.evidence: Only one output file written (the architecture .md); no save/persist action attempted. Footer line 174: 'Use the librarian skill to persist this artifact.' Source Breakdown (line 7) also notes librarian was unavailable and only suggests its use.

claims.claim: Amazon Chime SDK is HIPAA-eligible under the AWS BAA
claims.evidence: Amazon Chime SDK is a HIPAA-eligible AWS service; the output also correctly hedges by flagging re-verification against the current AWS HIPAA-eligible list (Research Suggestions).

claims.claim: No capabilities were invented — architecture anchors only to the five listed
claims.evidence: All five capabilities (registration, scheduling, video, prescriptions, billing) map 1:1 in the Capability→Tech table; recording/claims/e-prescribing scope deferred to Open Questions rather than added as features.

claims.claim: Externalizing payments via tokenization keeps card data out of the environment and minimizes PCI scope
claims.evidence: AD-03 (lines 125-130) correctly describes processor tokenization storing only tokens + invoice records; standard PCI scope-reduction pattern.

workarounds: Librarian and researcher skills were unavailable in this run; output notes this and provides ready-to-use researcher queries plus a librarian persistence suggestion instead.

suggestions.assertion: Output contains 'Tech Stack' / 'Capability → Tech Mapping' / 'Key Architecture Decisions' / 'Research Suggestions' section
suggestions.reason: These four are section-heading-presence checks. The skill's OUTPUT_FORMAT.md prescribes these exact headings, so they pass trivially whenever the template is followed and do not discriminate quality. Consider strengthening at least one to assert content (e.g., 'Capability → Tech Mapping maps all 5 stated capabilities with no invented rows').

suggestions.assertion: Does NOT attempt to persist/save the output — suggests librarian skill instead
suggestions.reason: Verifiable here only because a transcript/tool-log is absent and the footer text is present. With no transcript provided to the grader, a run that DID call a save tool but also printed the footer would still pass. Consider asserting against the transcript that no write-to-knowledge-store tool was invoked.

eval_feedback.overall: Assertions are well-aligned with the constraint-adaptation goal (AWS-only, HIPAA, Python are all meaningfully checked). The main weakness is several pure section-presence checks that pass by template-following; the substantive constraint assertions carry the discriminating weight.
